clue.text: Part of 20 that's fine and dandy

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on a pencil grade
dandy as an adjective means excellent, first-rate, which is ace

explanation.surface: Something is declared fine and dandy, all well and good.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 across is CLOCK, so 'Part of 20' is the dial with the numbers on it. 'Fine and dandy' reads as one stock phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The dial carrying the numbers and hands is a principal component of any timepiece.

clue.text: Solitary man guarding front of goal going into extra time

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it protectively, so these letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: a man who keeps to himself is a loner

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, here taken from goal

explanation.surface: A lone defender protects the goal as the match goes into extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture makes 'extra time' look like a sports term, but read plainly it just means lasting more time. G, the front of 'goal', sits inside LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extended past its normal span runs for a greater length of time, like a match with added minutes.

clue.text: Like mounted horse, most capably controlled by jockey

parts.note: doing something most capably is doing it best
a horse steered by a jockey is ridden

explanation.surface: A horse being ridden is at its best when a capable jockey is in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with a rider sitting astride it has been straddled, the adjective describing such a mount.

clue.text: Exciting female and I sound like 10 20

parts.note: 10 20 is ALARM CLOCK, and what an alarm clock does is ring

explanation.surface: Someone describes a thrilling woman and says they themselves go off like an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is ALARM and 20 across is CLOCK, so the cross-reference asks what noise an alarm clock makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stirring up enthusiasm, as in igniting the imagination, is to be stimulating or thrilling.

clue.text: Likely to respond and foolishly create about X's opposite number

indicators.note: one piece goes about, that is around, the other
doing something foolishly messes it up, so the letters of create are jumbled

parts.note: on a clock face numbered in Roman numerals, X (ten) sits directly across from IV (four)

explanation.surface: Someone liable to react foolishly creates trouble about an opponent identified as X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposite number' looks like a counterpart person, but on a Roman-numeral dial it is the numeral facing ten. 'about' puts it inside REACTE, the jumble that 'foolishly' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical or person prone to react to a stimulus is inclined to respond readily.

clue.text: Periods of time read from dial? Yes, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, of dial yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the time can be read from the dial, and the answer is yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spans of twenty-four hours are standard units by which time is measured.

clue.text: Hot stuff in a bar swallowed by brave person

indicators.note: something swallowed by another ends up inside it, so these letters go within the outer word

parts.note: a brave person is a hero
to bar something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A spicy drink in a bar is downed by a brave customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub in the surface but is the verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a very fiery chilli pepper, so 'hot stuff' describes it literally.

clue.text: Issue great healer raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom up, that is backwards

parts.note: from the saying that time is a great healer

explanation.surface: A matter concerning a great healer has been brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'time is a great healer' supplies the word; 'raised' turns it upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a sound or light is to send it out or give it off.

clue.text: Make amends with item reordered previously

parts.note: to make amends for a wrong is to atone

indicators.note: reordered means the letters of item are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone makes amends by sorting out an item as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reordered' turns ITEM into TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning formerly, once upon a time, so it can replace previously in a sentence.

clue.text: Flap like wings, 22 down

parts.note: alar is an adjective meaning relating to or like wings
22 down is MINUTE, abbreviated to M

explanation.surface: Something flaps like wings and goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' and 'wings' suggest a bird, but 'Flap' is the noun for a panic. ALAR is an uncommon word for wing-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a state of agitated panic, and a sudden fright or warning signal fits the same sense.

clue.text: See 21
Odd instances happening all the time

indicators.note: odd means peculiar or out of the ordinary, so the letters of instances are reshaped

explanation.surface: Strange occurrences keep happening all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never stops, continuing without pause, is going on constantly.

clue.text: Back rank chess piece is on

indicators.note: back means the word for rank is read backwards

parts.note: a rank is a line or row, as of soldiers
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A chess player notes which piece is standing on the back rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back rank' is a real chess term for the first row, which makes 'Back' hard to see as the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is on is functioning, operating as it should.

clue.text: Angry exchange using weapons second initially pulled out

indicators.note: the letter for second is pulled out from the start of the word for weapons

parts.note: swords are weapons

explanation.surface: In a heated quarrel, weapons were pulled out a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' says the S removed is the one at the front, not the one at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Having words with someone means arguing, so the plural noun names a heated quarrel.

clue.text: Test cricket, for example, filled with pressure

indicators.note: the first word is filled with, so holds inside it, the other letter

parts.note: a cricket is an example of an insect
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A Test cricket match is played under intense pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test cricket' is a long-form international match, but here 'Test' is the definition and the cricket is the chirping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to examine it closely, which is what checking or scrutinising means.

clue.text: What moves the middle row in a 22, used when connected

definitions.text: What moves the middle row in a 22
definitions.meaning: the thin pointer that sweeps round once every minute (22 down is MINUTE)
joined with a hyphen, the two words mean pre-owned, not new

explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is MINUTE. 'When connected' says to hyphenate the two words for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest pointer on a dial goes round once each minute; hyphenated, the phrase describes goods previously owned.

clue.text: Wine that's acceptable, if you lose little time opening it

indicators.note: the letter for time comes at the opening, the start, of the wine's name

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
acceptable means okay

explanation.surface: A wine is acceptable as long as you don't waste time opening it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: lose the T at the opening of the wine and what is left means acceptable. So the wine is T followed by OKAY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine from the Tokaj region.

clue.text: Drinks for some toast

definitions.meaning: a set of drinks bought for a group in a pub, one each
a slice of toast is called this, as in a plate of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' suggests raising a glass, linking with the drinks, but it is the grilled bread.
explanation.definitionFit: One purchase of drinks for everyone in a group, and a single slice of bread, share this word.

clue.text: Lacking experience, one's thrown out of everything and departs

indicators.note: one is thrown out of, removed from, the word for everything

parts.note: the universe is everything that exists
I is the Roman numeral one
D is the abbreviation for departs, as in timetables

explanation.surface: Someone inexperienced is thrown out of everything and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'one's thrown out', the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not versed in a subject has no knowledge or skill in it, so is inexperienced.

clue.text: Article shared by heathen, atheist and others

indicators.note: the same three letters are shared by, sitting inside, each of heathen, atheist and others

explanation.surface: A news article is shared by unbelievers and other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters appear in all three words, 'heathen', 'atheist' and 'others', not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the definite article is the commonest example of an article.

clue.text: Lovers meeting check out half past nine for this, finally

parts.note: to check something out is to try it

indicators.note: the second half of the word past is its last two letters
finally takes the last letter of each of nine, for and this

explanation.surface: Lovers check out at half past nine for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half past nine' looks like a time but splits: 'half' takes ST from PAST, and 'finally' takes the last letters of 'nine', 'for' and 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic rendezvous, so those who keep one are lovers who meet.

clue.text: Bird ingesting large bean or nut

indicators.note: the bird ingests, takes inside it, the other letter

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A bird eats a big bean or a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bean' and 'nut' are both British slang for the head, not food for the bird; to hit someone on the head is to give them one with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for a blow to the head, or the head itself, as bean and nut are.

clue.text: Old record sum produced by 13 17 19 20

definitions.meaning: a gramophone disc played at that many revolutions per minute, superseded by vinyl
13 17 19 20 reads WORKING ROUND THE CLOCK: add up every number round the dial, 1 to 12, and that is the total

explanation.walkthrough: The theme phrase is spread over four across lights. Adding 1+2+...+12 gives the total on a clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac discs spun at this speed before long-playing records; it is also the sum of one to twelve.

clue.text: Change to hymn, inserting line for publication

indicators.note: inserting means the letter for line goes into the rearranged letters
changing the words to and hymn means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: An editor alters a hymn by adding a line before it is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change to hymn' reads like an editorial instruction; 'publication' is a noun here, a magazine issued every month, not the act of publishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine issued once every four weeks or so is itself called by this noun.

clue.text: Mum is going outside home very little

indicators.note: one word goes outside, around, the other

parts.note: mum as an adjective means silent, as in keeping mum, so mute
in means at home

explanation.surface: Mother goes out of the house for a very short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but it means saying nothing, as in 'mum's the word'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiny is extremely small; the adjective is stressed on its second syllable.

clue.text: Beauties I perceived in answer crossing this one

indicators.note: the letter I is perceived in, seen inside, the other word

parts.note: 26 across, which crosses this light, is the parts of the day

explanation.surface: Someone sees beauties in a crossword answer that crosses this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossing answer is 26 across, which shares its first letter with this light.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition these are beautiful maidens of paradise, so beauties is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Left behind, eschew tea, as we hear, before bedtime?

indicators.note: before means this piece comes ahead of the next one

parts.note: to eschew something is to forgo it

indicators.note: as we hear means going by sound, so the word for the drink becomes the letter it sounds like

parts.note: the drink tea is pronounced like the letter T
ten o'clock is a typical bedtime; the question mark admits it is only an example

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their evening cup before going to bed and is forgotten about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer remembered or left without thought has been abandoned in the mind.

clue.text: Hand in certain position is shown in paper, daily

indicators.note: the word is is shown inside the abbreviation for the paper

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times, is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A hand gesture appears in a daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand with fingers curled tight into the palm is the position meant.

clue.text: Rings from East London — 10 call?

indicators.note: a Cockney from East London drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: hoops are rings

explanation.surface: Rings sound out from East London, like an alarm call.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is ALARM, so '10 call' is an alarmed cry; the question mark marks it as a playful definition. Cockney speech, of East London, drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of dismay after a mistake is a cry of alarm or apology.

clue.text: Parts of day shared by Brendan and solvers, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals a word said aloud: the possessive sounds like the units of time when the h is silent

parts.note: Brendan is the setter, so what belongs to setter and solvers together is ours

explanation.surface: The setter remarks on the time of day he and his solvers spend together.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan is the setter's pseudonym, so the clue is talking about the setter and you, the solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: The day divides into twenty-four sixty-minute units, each one of its parts.

clue.text: Tiny moving parts visible in old timepiece

definitions.text: Tiny moving parts visible in old timepiece

parts.words: Tiny moving parts visible in old timepiece
parts.note: the old timepiece is an hourglass, whose fine grains can be watched trickling through its glass neck

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving parts' suggests cogs in a mechanism, but the old timepiece is an hourglass and the parts are its grains.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny grains flowing through an hourglass are the material of beaches and deserts.

clue.text: Kind of 15, one often dirty? It could be clean

definitions.meaning: a continuously moving pointer that glides round the dial, rather than ticking, carries this name
a chimney cleaner, often covered in soot
a clean one is a total victory or removal of everyone

explanation.walkthrough: 15 down is SECOND HAND. Three separate senses share the word, in three stretches of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a smoothly gliding pointer, a soot-covered chimney cleaner, and a complete win.

clue.text: Revise rent, I note, or enter into continued possession

indicators.note: to revise is to rework, so the letters of rent I note are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenant revises the rent and makes a note, or moves in to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: A double anagram: 'or enter into' gives the same nine letters, so either fodder works and 'or' offers the alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping hold of something over time is to retain it, so the noun means ongoing holding.
